baseline.note: The measurement head differs from sourceHead only by the MIG5B ledger-close commit.

startup.note: Each warm-start stage ceiling is its merged-base maximum times eight plus 750 ms of cross-runner jitter. The first matrix launch is a separately bounded cold start; at most two of the remaining 26 launches may exceed their stage ceilings, no warm timing may exceed four seconds, and no cold timing may exceed ten seconds.

bundleBudgetRevisions.reason: IM platform setup, gateway deployment instructions and group member controls add 1.23% CSS. The previous 315000-byte ceiling had only 7 bytes of headroom at baseHead. The 320000-byte CSS ceiling keeps 1124 bytes of headroom; JavaScript, shared UI, gallery, startup and workload ceilings are unchanged. Both renderer revisions were measured with the same Vite production pipeline and installed dependencies; shared UI CSS is identical between these revisions.

Screenshot alignment across usage, capabilities, settings, IM, grouped tool calls, the breathing plan capsule, goal rail and Agent panels adds 2.86% CSS. The previous 305000-byte limit had 67 bytes of headroom at baseHead. The 315000-byte CSS ceiling keeps 1347 bytes of headroom; JavaScript, shared UI, gallery and startup ceilings are unchanged. Measurements use the same Vite production pipeline with HEAD renderer and shared CSS substituted for the baseline.

Full 9556fac prototype migration adds integrated navigation, rail/peek structure, composer and goal treatments, context colors, and 20 optional semantic token fallbacks. Isolated builds with identical installed dependencies measure 319175 bytes before and 337772 bytes after (+18597, 5.83%). The 342000-byte ceiling leaves 4228 bytes of headroom. JavaScript, shared UI, gallery, startup and workload ceilings remain unchanged.

startupBudgetRevisions.reason: The shared baseline was measured on macOS arm64. In this Windows run all 27 launches remained below the unchanged 4000 ms warm hard maximum, but five variants crossed derived stage ceilings. A 250 ms jitter correction leaves two bounded core-state outliers rather than five. The baseline multiplier, two-outlier allowance, 10000 ms cold hard maximum, bundle budgets and workload budgets are unchanged; the earlier 7545 ms startup still fails.
